title: Everything Is Right! Except This... Yoeleo G21 Altera Gravel Bike First Look

takeaways.text: Supplied free by Yoeleo. Packaging was the best the reviewer had seen, with every hardware item bagged and a clear manual with torque values; hose and wire routing through the headset and bar rated about 6/10.
45 mm Pirelli Cinturato Gravel H tires left plenty of room in the frame and fork; the reviewer cites Yoeleo's 53 mm maximum but did not test it.
The current frame takes a round seatpost, so dropper or suspension posts fit (the previous version used a D-shaped post); routing, T47 bottom bracket and drop stays noted.
The in-frame storage bags are tight to pack and refit, and the plastic latch looked fragile to the reviewer.

Yoeleo lists a 42T maximum chainring. A 48T only fitted with spacers behind the crank and sat very close to the chainstay, and a left-arm crank power meter touched the chainstay, so it could not be used.

At 170 cm the reviewer chose a 52 cm frame because the integrated bar comes no longer than 115 mm or narrower than 40 cm; the frame felt large and he would have preferred the smaller size with a longer bar.
First ride on sand, rock gardens and fast gravel: relaxed, stable and comfortable, less agile in slow turns, and controlled in crosswinds with 45 mm-deep wheels. Rated 7.8/10 overall.

disclosure: The reviewer says Yoeleo sent the bike for free without editorial control; the description has affiliate discount links.
summary: First-look review covering unboxing, features, storage, fit and a first gravel ride, with sizing and integrated-bar choices discussed in detail.
